newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian judge reschedules Rao cheating hearing.
newsitem.headline: Indian judge reschedules Rao cheating hearing.

text.p: An Indian judge on Wednesday postponed a hearing into accusations of criminal cheating by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao until next week, United News of India (UNI) said.
Special Judge Ajit Bharihoke had scheduled a hearing in the case, one of two involving Rao, for Wednesday.
But the Supreme Court has yet to rule on a police request for the venue of the hearing to be shifted from Bharihoke's courtroom in a crowded local court complex to a more secure location.
Bharihoke rescheduled the hearing for October 16, the newsagency said.
In a separate case of alleged forgery, Delhi High Court Judge S.K. Mahajan was set to rule on Wednesday on a request by Rao for legal protection against arrest.
Mahajan was expected to announce his decision shortly after 2 p.m. (0830 GMT).
In the cheating case, the Supreme Court was expected to rule on the request for a change in venue by the end of the week, court officials said.

Police said last week that they could not guarantee Rao's safety if he appeared in the Tis Hazari court complex, and they suggested the hearing be shifted to a large government-owned conference hall which could hold hundreds of journalists.
An Indian expatriate businessman, Lakhubhai Pathak, has alleged Rao and a Hindu guru named Chandraswami conspired to cheat him of $100,000 in 1983. Rao says he is innocent.
